text: CLI auto-discovery. doeff run finds the interpreter and the environments for your program.
A program only yields effects. Which handlers answer them is decided when it runs.
Without discovery, every command names the interpreter and the environments. With markers, the program is enough.
Mark a function with the comment: doeff, interpreter, default. It becomes a default interpreter.
Mark a variable that has a type annotation with: doeff, default. It becomes a default environment.
doeff-indexer scans the source and lists every marked symbol. A variable without an annotation is skipped.
doeff run cuts the program's module path into a hierarchy, from the root package down.
It keeps only the interpreters marked on that path: in the program's own module, or in a package above it.
Two are on the path. base interpreter, at index zero, and auth interpreter, at index two.
The closest one, the deepest, wins. auth interpreter will run the program.
Environments are not chosen. Every marked environment on the path is collected, root first.
They merge from left to right. A later value overrides an earlier one.
timeout is ten in base env, twenty in features env, and thirty in auth env. Thirty wins.
The merged environment keeps every key from all three.
Then doeff run calls auth interpreter with the program, and the merged environment as env.
The interpreter installs its handlers around the program. reader holds the merged environment.
login yields Ask for the database host, then Ask for the timeout. reader answers each one, and k resumes.
The program never named a handler or a config file. It returns: localhost, timeout thirty.
To run the same program with something else, say so on the command line.
The env flag replaces the discovered environments. auth interpreter is still discovered, and answers from the fake one.
The interpreter flag turns off discovery of both. With no env flag, the first Ask fails.
Both flags warn that they are deprecated. The hy flag composes the handlers inline instead.
And if no marked interpreter is on the path? doeff run does not stop. It uses its built-in default interpreter.
It ignores environments, so Ask for the timeout finds no handler. format json shows what was chosen.
Markers keep handlers next to the code. doeff run finds them by where the program lives.
